name: Outgoing Webhooks
description: Subscriber-configured outbound webhooks (tenant-scoped; root tenant carries platform-wide events), signed deliveries, retry+redelivery.
author: Kuray Karaaslan

extensions.description: Encrypts the webhook signing secrets (secret, previousSecret) stored before the columns were field-encrypted (P9-6): idempotent, batched, guarded on the value read, counts only. New writes are encrypted by the entity transformer. Also runs on every dedicated tenant database of the deploy fan-out (metadata.tenantDatabases), where a tenant with a database of its own keeps these rows.
Webhook signing secrets (secret, previousSecret), encrypted under the tenant's data key (P7-TDEK, F16).

Every 10 minutes: re-enqueues the PENDING webhook deliveries whose BullMQ job was lost (Redis lost its data), with the delivery id as the job id; dead-letters, with a reason, those older than a day or whose endpoint is gone or disabled (D252, docs/audits/2026-11-03-redis-outage.md §6.8). HTTP twin: POST /api/cron/webhook-pending-sweep.

Phase 55: the signal kinds this module emits (the audit actions it owns: a webhook endpoint created, updated, deleted and its signing secret rotated; deliveries redelivered, dead letters replayed, tests sent and events triggered by hand), each attribute with its personal-data class. Read by ai_firewall through its registry; imports only the contract from common.

metadata.label: webhook: endpoints created, changed, deleted and their secret rotated; deliveries redelivered, replayed, tested and triggered (phase 55 coverage)

extensionPoints.description: A module declares a webhook event it emits, without editing webhook: one contribution per event, the contribution key is the event name (lower-case dotted segments, stable forever) and the static metadata is { scope: 'tenant' | 'platform', group, label, description }. The export is the module's <module>.webhook-events file, which lists the names for its emit sites; only the metadata is read, so building the catalog loads no code. The catalog (webhook.catalog.ts) is process-wide: the events of every installed module, whatever a tenant has switched on. Create, update and the manual trigger refuse an event no installed module declares for the tenant's scope (422); an update may keep an already-stored event whose module was removed. A dispatched event nobody declares is logged once and skips the endpoint lookup (event sinks still hear it). Two modules may declare the same event; the first by order wins and a declaration with a different scope is ignored with a warning.

A module that wants to hear every dispatched domain event. Default export: { key?, names?: string[], onEvent(tenantId, event, payload, meta?) } where meta is { actor?: { type, id } } (only the actor id travels; a flow that needs a name reads it with an enrichment node). dispatchEvent calls it BEFORE the plan gate, FIRE-AND-FORGET: dispatchEvent sits on the request path of ~50 modules, so a sink that is slow, broken or missing must never delay or fail a dispatch. A tenant without the feature_webhooks plan feature still reaches its sinks (the sink applies its own plan gate). Each sink is isolated; a throw is logged and dropped. Platform-scope events are pinned to the root tenant by dispatchPlatformEvent, so sinks hear them under the root tenant only.
